Salicylaldehyde, a naturally occurring aromatic aldehyde found in plant-derived preparations, remains poorly characterized regarding its vascular effects. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to evaluate the vasorelaxant and antihypertensive properties of salicylaldehyde and to elucidate its underlying mechanisms of action. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Molecular docking was performed to assess interactions with key vascular targets. In vitro vasorelaxant activity was investigated using isolated rat thoracic aortic rings precontracted with epinephrine (EP, 10 μM) or potassium chloride (KCl, 80 mM). The involvement of endothelium-dependent and independent pathways was examined using pharmacological inhibitors and angiotensin II-induced contraction assays. In vivo effects were evaluated following oral administration of salicylaldehyde (20 and 40 mg/kg) in normotensive and N-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester (L-NAME)-induced hypertensive rats. Blood pressure was measured using a tail-cuff system during acute (6 h) and sub-chronic (7 days) treatments. RESULTS: Salicylaldehyde showed strong binding affinities toward angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) and angiotensin II Type 1 Receptor. It induced concentration-dependent vasorelaxation, significantly reduced after endothelial removal and under KCl-induced contraction. Its effects were attenuated by inhibitors of ACE, ACE2, ATP-sensitive K+ channels, and L-type calcium channels, and it inhibited angiotensin II-induced contraction. In vivo, it significantly reduced systolic and diastolic blood pressure in hypertensive rats. CONCLUSION: Salicylaldehyde exerts antihypertensive effects via multiple mechanisms and may contribute to the cardiovascular activity of plant-derived remedies.

articles.title: Impact of nonspecific binding to membrane vesicles on unbound IC50 estimation for P-glycoprotein and breast cancer resistance protein inhibitors and implications for drug-drug interaction risk assessment.
articles.abstract: P-glycoprotein and breast cancer resistance protein are key efflux transporters relevant to drug-drug interactions (DDIs) for orally administered drugs. The International Council for Harmonisation of Technical Requirements for Pharmaceuticals for Human Use M12 guidance recommends using unbound in vitro inhibition potency (IC50,u) for clinical risk assessment, yet the influence of nonspecific binding to membrane vesicles remains uncharacterized. Herein, vesicle binding for a panel of efflux transporter inhibitors was systematically quantified using equilibrium dialysis and compared with conventional microsomal binding. Nonspecific binding to vesicles reduced free inhibitor concentrations, resulting in right-shifted IC50 values, particularly for high-binding compounds (itraconazole and dronedarone) compared with low-binding compounds (telmisartan) in breast cancer resistance protein assays with Sf9 control vesicles. Similar right shifts were observed for P-glycoprotein inhibition assays with human embryonic kidney 293 control vesicles, although less pronounced. Correction of IC50 values across different vesicle concentrations generally resulted in aligned IC50,u values. Microsomal binding correlated strongly (Pearson correlation coefficient = 0.965) with vesicle binding, supporting its use as a surrogate for binding correction. Incorporating binding-corrected IC50 values into static DDI risk calculations increased false positives but did not affect false negatives. These findings demonstrate that accounting for fraction unbound in vesicle-based assays can substantially influence the estimation of in vitro inhibitory potency and subsequent static DDI risk assessment. SIGNIFICANT STATEMENT: This study systematically characterizes nonspecific binding to membrane vesicles in P-glycoprotein and breast cancer resistance protein inhibition assays and demonstrates its substantial impact on IC50 determination. The strong correlation between vesicles and microsomal binding provides a practical surrogate for implementing International Council for Harmonisation of Technical Requirements for Pharmaceuticals for Human Use M12 unbound potency recommendations for vesicle-based inhibition assays.

articles.title: Functional characterization of rare DPYD variants identified in 8,380 Japanese individuals: implications for 5-fluorouracil metabolism.
articles.abstract: Dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPD) is the rate-limiting enzyme in the metabolism of 5-fluorouracil, and reduced DPD activity resulting from DPYD genetic variants is a major cause of severe 5-fluorouracil -induced toxicity. Although several clinically relevant variants have been identified in Caucasian populations, the functional consequences of rare DPYD variants identified in Japanese individuals remain poorly characterized. In this study, we comprehensively analyzed 26 DPYD variants identified through whole-genome sequencing of 8380 Japanese individuals. Recombinant DPD proteins were expressed in 293FT cells, and enzymatic activity was evaluated using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry to determine kinetic parameters (Km, Vmax, CLint). Protein expression levels and quaternary structure were assessed by immunoblotting and blue native PAGE, and structural modeling was performed to explore possible structural consequences of selected variants. Among the 26 DPD variants analyzed, 5 exhibited markedly reduced or abolished enzymatic activity compared with wild-type DPD, including 3 loss of function variants. Loss of detectable homodimer formation was observed in Gly194Asp and Glu386Ter, whereas other functionally impaired variants retained homodimer formation, indicating that altered dimerization represents only one potential mechanism contributing to DPD dysfunction. Structural analyses suggested possible local alterations affecting cofactor interactions or the dimer interface in selected variants, providing hypotheses for future mechanistic investigation. These findings provide a comprehensive functional characterization of rare DPYD variants identified in Japanese individuals and support their prioritization for future clinical validation. However, their clinical significance and potential utility for fluoropyrimidine dose individualization require confirmation in patients receiving fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy. SIGNIFICANT STATEMENT: This study functionally characterized 26 rare DPYD variants identified in a Japanese population and identified 5 variants with markedly reduced or abolished DPD activity. These findings expand the functional annotation of DPYD variation in a population in which established fluoropyrimidine-associated risk variants are uncommon and provide evidence to prioritize functionally impaired variants for future clinical validation.

articles.title: Redox-mitochondrial-epigenetic network disruption and its intergenerational impact in zebrafish: Protective effects of metformin.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Oxidative stress is a central mechanism of chronic toxicity, disrupting metabolic, inflammatory, apoptotic, mitochondrial, and epigenetic processes. Potassium bromate (KBrO₃) induces oxidative stress, but its systemic effects following chronic exposure and modulation by metformin remain insufficiently characterized. This study evaluated chronic KBrO₃ toxicity in zebrafish, the effects of concurrent metformin exposure, and molecular responses in F1 offspring following parental exposure. METHODS: Adult zebrafish were exposed to KBrO₃ for 28 days with or without metformin co-treatment. Histopathological analyses of liver, ovary, intestine, and testis were performed. IL-1β, insulin, and vitellogenin were analyzed by ELISA, wheras oxidative stress, metabolic, inflammatory, apoptotic, and epigenetic markers by qPCR. Global DNA methylation, mitochondrial DNA copy number, and relative telomere length were evaluated in F0 and F1 cohorts. Data were analyzed using conventional statistics, principal component analysis, and Spearman correlation. RESULTS: KBrO₃ exposure was associated with alterations in antioxidant defence, metabolism, inflammation, apoptosis, mitochondrial and epigenetic endpoints, and tissue pathology. Metformin co-treatment attenuated multiple KBrO₃-associated molecular and histopathological alterations. In F1 offspring, selected gene-expression and DNA methylation alterations were observed, whereas mtDNA copy number and relative telomere length did not differ significantly among groups, indicating endpoint-specific intergenerational responses. Multivariate analyses identified coordinated biomarker patterns associated with treatment. CONCLUSION: Chronic KBrO₃ exposure produced coordinated molecular and tissue alterations, while metformin co-treatment attenuated several associated responses. Selected F1 molecular and epigenetic alterations indicate intergenerational responses following parental exposure, although F2/F3 generations were not assessed. These findings support further investigation of metformin as a pharmacological modulator of oxidative stress-associated toxicity.

articles.title: Insights into osteoporosis triggered by common antiepileptic drugs via network toxicology, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Antiepileptic drugs (AEDs), first-line treatments for epilepsy and related seizure disorders, are increasingly recognized as important risk factors for osteoporosis. However, the molecular mechanisms and specific targets underlying AED-induced bone loss remain largely unclear. METHODS: We explored these mechanisms using an integrated strategy combining network toxicology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and in vitro experiments. Common targets of four AEDs and osteoporosis were identified through database screening, followed by protein-protein interaction network construction, hub gene identification, and functional enrichment analysis. Molecular docking was used to evaluate the predicted binding affinity between AEDs and primary hub targets, and 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations were applied to assess dynamic binding stability. Furthermore, colony formation assays and Western blots were performed in MC3T3-E1 pre-osteoblasts to support the computational predictions. RESULTS: We identified 47, 50, 46, and 48 potential osteoporosis-related targets for carbamazepine phenobarbital phenytoin (PHT), and valproic acid respectively. These targets were mainly enriched in key signaling pathways and cellular processes associated with bone metabolism. Topological analysis identified four primary hub targets: epidermal growth factor receptor, CASP3, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma, and PTGS2. AEDs and their targets exhibited favorable binding affinity in the molecular docking simulations (binding energy < -5 kcal/mol). Molecular dynamics simulations revealed heterogeneous dynamic stability among the complexes: PB-CASP3 and PHT-PPARG reached relatively stable conformational equilibrium, whereas CBZ-EGFR displayed notable protein residue flexibility in the equilibrated trajectory, and VPA-PTGS2 sustained persistent structural fluctuations during the simulation period. In vitro experiments demonstrated that all AEDs inhibited the clonogenic capacity of MC3T3-E1 cells, and Western blot results further indicated that AEDs differentially modulated the expression and activation levels of their corresponding primary hub targets, which was consistent with the computational predictions. CONCLUSION: This study constructs an integrated research framework combining computational prediction and in vitro validation to explore potential molecular mechanisms underlying AED-induced osteoblast dysfunction and osteoporosis. The findings highlight candidate targets and provide a preliminary mechanistic basis for future rational clinical medication and skeletal protection in patients receiving long-term AED therapy.

articles.title: Targeting the PCSK9-PR-IL-17 axis for psoriasis therapy.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Psoriasis is a chronic, immune-mediated inflammatory dermatosis characterized by keratinocyte hyperproliferation and systemic metabolic comorbidities. Although proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) is a well-established regulator of lipid metabolism, its role in the cutaneous inflammatory microenvironment remains poorly defined. This study investigated the contribution of PCSK9 to psoriatic inflammation and its potential underlying mechanisms. METHODS: PCSK9 expression was assessed in human psoriatic lesions and an imiquimod (IMQ)-induced mouse model. The effects of pharmacological PCSK9 inhibition with SBC-110736 were evaluated using PASI-like scores and inflammatory cell infiltration. Transcriptomic analysis was performed to identify associated signaling pathways. The relationship between PCSK9 and progesterone receptor (PR) expression in keratinocytes and the effects of the PR agonist progesterone were also examined. RESULTS: PCSK9 expression was significantly upregulated in human psoriatic lesions and in the IMQ-induced mouse model. SBC-110736 attenuated psoriasis-like disease severity, reducing PASI-like scores and infiltration of CD4+ and CD11b+ cells. Transcriptomic analysis indicated that PCSK9 inhibition primarily suppressed interleukin-17 (IL-17) signaling while restoring Pgr expression. PCSK9 and PR expression were inversely associated in keratinocytes, suggesting that PCSK9-mediated PR downregulation may exacerbate IL-17-driven inflammation. Progesterone treatment produced similar therapeutic effects to those observed with PCSK9 inhibition. DISCUSSION: These findings suggest that a PCSK9-PR-IL-17 axis contributes to psoriasis pathogenesis, with PR potentially serving as an endogenous anti-inflammatory brake. Targeting this pathway may offer a strategy to modulate cutaneous inflammation, while its potential effects on related metabolic disturbances warrant further investigation.

articles.title: Berberine suppresses mechanical stretch-induced apoptosis and proliferation in vascular smooth muscle cells via ROS/PDI/Drp1 signaling pathway.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) exhibit heterogeneous responses to mechanical stretch stress (SS), with some undergoing apoptosis and others proliferating. The mechanisms underlying this differential fate decision remain unclear. OBJECTIVE: This study investigated whether SS-induced heterogeneity in F-actin expression dictates distinct mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) responses, leading to different VSMC fates, and evaluated the therapeutic potential of the berberine (BBR). METHODS: VSMCs were subjected to SS. F-actin heterogeneity was characterized, and mitochondrial ROS (mtROS), proliferation, and apoptosis were assessed. The involvement of the PKCα/PDI/Drp1 signaling axis was examined using pharmacological inhibitors and BBR. RESULTS: SS induced heterogeneous mtROS production in VSMCs with varying F-actin levels. This differential ROS signaling concurrently activated the pro-proliferative mTOR/p70 pathway and the pro-apoptotic caspase-9/3 cascade via the PKCα/PDI/Drp1 axis. Importantly, BBR treatment effectively attenuated both SS-induced proliferation and apoptosis by suppressing PKCα activation and subsequent mitochondrial signaling. CONCLUSION: Our findings reveal that F-actin heterogeneity determines VSMC fate under SS by driving distinct mitochondrial ROS responses. BBR, by counteracting these ROS-dependent pathways, emerges as a promising therapeutic strategy for managing stretch-related vascular pathologies, such as hypertension-induced atherosclerosis.

articles.title: High-affinity ELR+ CXC chemokines display balanced G protein-, GRK- and β-arrestin-associated transducer engagement at the viral G protein-coupled receptor ORF74.
articles.abstract: Open reading frame 74 (ORF74) is the single G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) encoded in the genome of Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV). Due to its high constitutive activity and broad chemokine binding profile, ORF74 contributes to KSHV-associated diseases through autocrine and paracrine mechanisms that promote cell proliferation, inflammation and angiogenesis. Previous studies showed that ELR+ CXC chemokines (i.e., CXCL1-3 and CXCL5-8), which contain a conserved Glu-Leu-Arg motif, bind ORF74 with high affinity. Among these chemokines, CXCL1-3 and CXCL6-8 act as full or partial agonists in ORF74-mediated G protein signaling and β-arrestin recruitment, whereas CXCL5 behaves as a neutral ligand. However, whether these chemokines preferentially engage specific intracellular transducers remains unclear. We therefore applied a unified NanoLuc Binary Technology (NanoBiT) platform in HEK293A cells to systematically compare how ELR+ CXC chemokines modulate ORF74-transducer proximity across the G protein-GRK-β-arrestin axis. CXCL1-3 and CXCL6-8, but not CXCL5, induced concentration-dependent ORF74-specific responses involving miniGi recruitment, Gβ1 proximity, GRK2/3/5/6 proximity and β-arrestin1/2 recruitment. Using CXCL1 as the reference ligand, bias analysis showed that the active ELR+ CXC chemokines engage ORF74 in a largely balanced manner across these proximal transducer readouts.

articles.title: Exploratory pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic range of tigecycline for balancing treatment effect and safety in hospital-acquired pneumonia: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Tigecycline (TGC) is a core antibiotic for treating hospital-acquired pneumonia (HAP) caused by multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria, but the absence of individualized dosing guidance that balances treatment effect and safety frequently results in suboptimal efficacy or coagulation-related adverse events in clinical practice. METHODS: A single-center retrospective study was conducted, enrolling 100 patients with MDR-HAP who were assigned to a standard-dose group or a high-dose group based on clinical decisions. The efficacy and safety of different TGC dosing regimens were compared between the two groups. RESULTS: The trough concentration (Cmin), intermediate concentration (C1/2), and peak concentration (Cmax), the estimated ratio of the area under the concentration-time curve to the 24h of dosing/minimum inhibitory concentration (eAUIC), pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) target attainment rate, clinical response rate and overall favorable outcome rate in the high-dose group were significantly higher than those in the standard group (p < 0.05). The incidence of thrombocytopenia was significantly higher in the high-dose group (36.67% vs. 17.14%, p = 0.034), whereas the incidence of hypofibrinogenemia was numerically higher but did not reach statistical significance (40.0% vs. 30.0%, p = 0.330). No significant between-group differences were observed in microbiological eradication rate, median survival time, 30-day all-cause mortality, coagulation parameters, gastrointestinal reactions, or liver function damage. Binary logistic regression analysis revealed that eAUIC [OR = 1.394 (1.135-1.712), p = 0.002] was an influencing predictor associated with clinical treatment effect. The area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve for eAUIC was 0.813, with a maximum Youden index of 0.557. The corresponding critical value was determined to be 2.915, with a sensitivity of 96.9% and a specificity of 58.8%. Furthermore, eAUIC was independently associated with both hypofibrinogenemia and thrombocytopenia. We identified an exploratory candidate eAUIC range of 2.915 - 3.565 that was associated with both clinical treatment effect and coagulation-related adverse events. DISCUSSION: This eAUIC range was derived from retrospective data and should be framed explicitly as a hypothesis to be tested, clinical applicability requires confirmation through prospective studies and external validation. Therapeutic drug monitoring may assist in optimizing therapy, but prospective studies are needed to confirm these observations.

articles.title: Interpretable machine learning classifies β-lactamase subclasses and prioritizes boundary variants for antimicrobial resistance surveillance.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Antimicrobial resistance is a major global health threat, and β-lactamase-mediated inactivation of β-lactam antibiotics remains a leading cause of treatment failure. Rapid identification of emerging β-lactamase variants and improved understanding of their functional diversity are therefore essential for resistance surveillance and therapeutic development. METHODS: Here, we developed an interpretable machine learning framework to classify major Class A β-lactamase subclasses (TEM, SHV, and CTX-M) and distinguish them from non-β-lactamase hydrolases using multidimensional protein descriptors. Descriptors based on sequence composition, physicochemical properties, residue accessibility, and structural topology were evaluated to identify a minimal panel of 30 descriptors while preserving biological interpretability. RESULTS: The selected descriptors provided strong discriminatory power and were linked to steric environment, hydrophobicity, flexibility, solvent exposure, and residue interaction patterns, consistent with roles in substrate recognition and catalysis. Projection into reduced descriptor space identified transitional variants near subclass boundaries, including CTX-M/SHV convergence zones and non-β-lactamase hydrolases with partial β-lactamase-like signatures. Representative case studies indicated that some apparent misclassifications may reflect annotation inconsistencies, scaffold convergence, or early adaptive trajectories, highlighting candidates for experimental follow-up. External validation using 271 independent proteins annotated as non-β-lactamase hydrolases demonstrated 96.95% specificity, with only limited false-positive assignments. Most incorrect classifications showed weak statistical support, indicating that confidence filtering could further improve screening performance. DISCUSSION: Overall, this study demonstrates that compact descriptor-based models can provide accurate and interpretable classification of β-lactamase-related proteins while identifying emerging boundary variants relevant to antimicrobial resistance surveillance. The framework offers a scalable approach for protein annotation, monitoring resistance evolution, and supporting future inhibitor development.

articles.title: Value-based pricing of brensocatib for frequently exacerbating non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis in China: a China-adapted, FEV1-inclusive time-dependent markov analysis.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To estimate a China-specific value-based annual price (P*) for brensocatib 25 mg added to standard care (SC), compared with SC alone, in adults with frequently exacerbating non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis, and to assess how strongly the estimate depends on transferred assumptions linking forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1) to long-term outcomes. METHODS: A seven-state Markov cohort model with monthly cycles and a lifetime horizon was constructed from the Chinese healthcare system perspective. Chinese sources informed the target population, exacerbation burden, baseline microbiology, background mortality, resource use, costs, discounting, and decision context, while ASPEN supplied the exacerbation rate ratio (0.81) and annual FEV1 decline (24 mL with brensocatib 25 mg vs. 62 mL with placebo). In the base case, cohort-mean FEV1 was linked to utility and mortality through explicit external mappings. A prespecified structural sensitivity removed both mappings but retained the trial-observed exacerbation benefit. Costs and outcomes were discounted by 4.5% annually. The primary willingness-to-pay (WTP) threshold was CNY 200,000 per quality-adjusted life-year (QALY); uncertainty was examined with a paired 10,000-draw probabilistic sensitivity analysis (PSA). RESULTS: At an illustrative price of CNY 120,000/year, the FEV1-inclusive base case estimated an incremental cost of CNY 551,543, gains of 0.2761 QALYs and 0.3432 discounted life-years, and 0.57 fewer lifetime exacerbations. These results corresponded to an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of CNY 1,997,665/QALY and P* of CNY 11,692/year. Drug acquisition accounted for almost all of the incremental cost. The PSA median P* was CNY 11,611/year (95% simulation interval CNY 4,145-19,324), and none of 10,000 simulations was cost-effective at CNY 120,000/year for WTP thresholds up to CNY 300,000/QALY. Estimates changed little when China-specific demographic and exacerbation inputs were varied. In contrast, removing the FEV1-linked pathway reduced P* to CNY 990/year, while assuming persistent efficacy after attrition increased it to CNY 24,432/year. CONCLUSION: With inputs localised wherever credible Chinese evidence was available, the FEV1-inclusive base case estimated P* at CNY 11,692/year for a WTP of CNY 200,000/QALY. The broad pricing implication was stable, although the exact estimate depended chiefly on the durability and downstream consequences of the 52-week FEV1 difference. Both the base case and the key structural sensitivity remained far below the illustrative annual price of CNY 120,000.

articles.title: APOE4 differentially alters lipid composition in extracellular vesicles from hiPSC-derived neurons of Alzheimer's disease patients.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The Apolipoprotein E4 (APOE4) is the most significant genetic risk factor for late-onset Alzheimer's disease (AD), but the cellular mechanisms by which it increases vulnerability remain poorly understood. Lipids play a crucial role in membrane organization, vesicle trafficking, and inflammatory signaling in the brain. Increasing evidence suggests that changes in lipid metabolism might serve as a connection between genetic risk and neurodegeneration. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) reflect the lipidomic composition of their parent cell offering a window into lipidomic alterations that may be tracked in living humans over time. Given high variability in human samples, we sought to define APOE4-related lipidomic EV signatures in a controlled human cellular system. METHODS: We studied EVs secreted by four replicates of human-induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived glutamatergic neurons from two healthy individuals (APOE2/E3 and APOE4/4) and two patients with AD (APOE3/3 and APOE4/4). Targeted lipidomics enabled quantitative profiling of hundreds of individual lipid species across major lipid classes. Univariate and multivariate analyses were applied to identify lipid alterations associated with APOE genotype and AD status. RESULTS: APOE4 was associated with differences in lipid composition in neuronal EVs from both healthy and AD donors, suggesting that APOE4 influences EV lipid composition regardless of AD. Additionally, APOE4/4 carriers with AD exhibited clear, species-specific lipid imbalances. Lower levels of ganglioside GM3 and higher of phosphatidylserine emerged as consistent contributors to the APOE4-associated AD lipid signature, alongside alterations in dihydrosphingomyelin and phosphatidylinositol species linked to membrane integrity, endolysosomal function, and inflammatory pathways. These lipid species were among the strongest variables distinguishing healthy and AD APOE4/4 samples in multivariate analyses. CONCLUSION: These findings specify lipidomic changes in AD related to the APOE4 genotype, and support a model by which APOE4 creates a lipid profile that becomes selectively dysregulated in AD. By identifying specific lipid species associated with APOE4 and AD, this work provides further evidence that distinct lipidomic signatures are associated with both APOE4 and AD. These findings may contribute to the identification of lipid-based biomarkers and support future investigations into genotype-informed therapeutic strategies, although validation in larger, independent cohorts is required.

articles.title: Rituximab with low-dose glucocorticoids for treating refractory membranous nephropathy: a prospective single-center cohort study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Rituximab (RTX) is the first-line treatment for primary membranous nephropathy (pMN), yet approximately one-third of patients exhibit refractory disease. Evidence supporting RTX combined with low-dose glucocorticoids for refractory pMN remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of this combination regimen in a rituximab-naïve refractory cohort. METHODS: Thirty-six adults with refractory pMN received rituximab plus low-dose glucocorticoids (prednisone equivalent). The primary endpoint was clinical remission at 24 months, analyzed in both the intention-to-treat (ITT, n = 36) and per-protocol (PP, n = 22) populations. Sensitivity analyses included a worst-case scenario (assuming all dropouts were non-remitters). RESULTS: Thirty-five patients had evaluable 12-month outcomes, and 26 of them achieved remission (74.3%, with 25.7% achieving complete remission and 48.6% partial remission). By 24 months, the remission rate was 95.5% (21/22) in the per-protocol analysis and 91.67% in the intention-to-treat analysis, compared with 58.3% (21/36) in the worst-case scenario. We found no statistically significant difference in cumulative remission rates between serum PLA2R-positive and PLA2R-negative groups, or between renal tissue PLA2R-positive and PLA2R-negative groups. All 25 patients positive for anti-PLA2R antibodies showed a decreasing antibody trend after treatment, and 80.0% (20/25) achieved complete antibody clearance (antibody titer <20 RU/mL). Adverse events occurred in 37.1% (13/35) of patients, with 11.4% (4/35) of patients developing serious infections. No serious malignant events or fatal events were reported during the study. CONCLUSION: In this cohort of patients with refractory pMN, rituximab combined with low-dose glucocorticoids achieved high short-term remission rates, and no safety signals were observed that would preclude further investigation. However, given the uncontrolled study design, repeated RTX dosing, and residual confounding from prior immunosuppression, we cannot draw definitive conclusions on whether adding glucocorticoids offers incremental benefit compared with rituximab monotherapy. The high remission rates observed in this study may also be attributable to repeated rituximab exposure and residual effects of prior immunosuppression. Furthermore, this empirical combination regimen was not designed to test whether glucocorticoids have a direct additive or synergistic effect. Larger randomized controlled trials are therefore warranted to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Ocular safety signals of sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor modulators in postmarketing surveillance.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) receptor modulators are used for immune-mediated diseases, and macular oedema is an established ocular adverse effect. However, ocular-focused, class-wide postmarketing reporting across all five approved agents remains incompletely characterized. METHODS: We analyzed U.S. Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) data from 2004 Q1 through 2026 Q1 using report-level deduplication, approval-aligned windows, and primary-suspect exposure. Ocular events were assessed using a curated set of 52 Preferred Term (PT) strings. Sensitivity analyses included report-level macular/retinal oedema aggregation, same-indication active comparators, temporal and sparse-data analyses, restricted empirical-Bayes assessment, and external validation in Canada Vigilance. Exact-date time to onset was assessed for the aggregated phenotype. RESULTS: The primary cohort included 98,843 primary-suspect reports, of which 8,812 (8.9%) were ocular, representing 12,088 unique ocular report-PT pairs. At the class level, 21 ocular PTs met primary signal criteria; macular oedema showed the strongest anatomically specific signal (n = 947; reporting odds ratio [ROR], 48.18; 95% confidence interval [CI], 44.84-51.76). Fingolimod had the broadest signal spectrum; macular oedema was the principal anatomically specific signal for siponimod and ozanimod. No ponesimod PT met primary criteria, and the etrasimod macular oedema estimate was sparse (n = 11). Of 36 primary drug-PT signals, 13 were High, 22 Moderate, and one Low. Report-level aggregation yielded a class-level ROR of 29.47 (95% CI, 27.62-31.45). In indication-restricted multiple sclerosis analyses, the association remained elevated versus all non-S1P disease-modifying therapies (ROR, 43.85; 95% CI, 35.75-53.78), while ulcerative colitis/inflammatory bowel disease analyses were sparse and exploratory. For fingolimod, the association persisted after exclusion of the first two post-approval years (ROR, 45.79; 95% CI, 37.26-56.26). Median time to onset was 93.0 days for fingolimod and 15.5 days for siponimod. Canada Vigilance showed a concordant class-level association (ROR, 74.00; 95% CI, 59.30-92.35). CONCLUSION: Macular/retinal oedema was the most consistent ocular reporting pattern in the S1P receptor modulator class. The association remained evident after phenotype aggregation and indication-restricted analysis and was also observed in Canada Vigilance. Sparse data for newer agents and residual confounding limit comparative interpretation.

articles.title: Interaction of major monoterpenes from Rosmarinus officinalis L. essential oil with the human serotonin transporter: molecular docking, radioligand binding, and functional uptake studies.
articles.abstract: Major depressive disorder remains a leading cause of disability worldwide, and current antidepressants are limited by delayed therapeutic onset, incomplete efficacy, and adverse effects. Although Rosmarinus officinalis L. essential oil and its major monoterpenes exhibit antidepressant-like and anxiolytic properties, their molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated whether the principal rosemary monoterpenes, α-pinene, camphor, and 1,8-cineole, directly interact with the human serotonin transporter (hSERT) and its functional effects. Molecular docking simulations targeting the orthosteric (S1) and allosteric (S2) binding sites were combined with [3H]-paroxetine binding displacement assays and SERT-mediated uptake experiments based on the fluorescent serotonin analog FFN246 in HEK293 cells expressing YFP-tagged hSERT. Docking analyses predicted plausible binding poses for all three monoterpenes within both the S1 and S2 regions, although with less favorable docking scores than fluoxetine. Radioligand displacement assays provided experimental evidence that all three compounds interact with hSERT, producing concentration-dependent displacement of [3H]-paroxetine, with α-pinene displaying the highest potency, followed by 1,8-cineole and camphor. Functional assays further showed that all monoterpenes produced significant but incomplete inhibition of transporter-mediated FFN246 uptake, even at high micromolar concentrations, indicating partial rather than complete transporter blockade. Together, these findings identify hSERT as a previously unrecognized molecular target of rosemary monoterpenes, suggesting that these compounds may act as partial inhibitors of serotonin transport. These results provide new molecular insights into the potential mechanism that may contribute to the reported neurobehavioral effects of rosemary, and support further investigation of these compounds in serotonergic signaling and neurotransmission.

articles.title: Real-world effectiveness of pain pharmacotherapy for caesarean section in a low- and middle-income setting: A multicentre cross-sectional study in Ghana.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Effective analgesia is needed after caesarean section to enhance maternal health-related quality. Unfortunately, little is known about the realities on the ground in low-and middle-income countries. This study investigated the prevalent perioperative pharmacotherapeutic practices in Ghanaian healthcare settings for women undergoing elective caesarean section and their association with acute postoperative pain. METHOD: A multicentre cross-sectional study was conducted among 515 women who underwent elective caesarean section at four teaching hospitals in Ghana. Demographic and clinical data were collected using structured questionnaires and medical record reviews. Acute postoperative pain was assessed using the Numerical Pain Rating Scale (NRS) within the first 72 h after surgery. Data were analysed using R (Version 4.6.1). Statistical significance was defined as p < 0.05. RESULTS: Moderate to severe acute postoperative pain was reported by 60.0% (95% CI: 55.7%-64.1%) of participants despite widespread use of opioid-based analgesia. Multimodal analgesia was associated with significantly lower acute postoperative pain (OR = 0.34; 95% CI: 0.22-0.48; p < 0.001). The use of midazolam was associated with a 62% reduction in the odds of acute post-surgery pain (OR = 0.38; 95% Bootstrap CI: 0.20-0.63; p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: Multimodal analgesia was associated with superior postoperative pain control compared with opioid-based therapy alone; however, the persistently high prevalence of moderate to severe pain indicates substantial gaps in the implementation of contemporary pain management strategies during and following caesarean deliveries in Ghana.

articles.title: Nanotechnology meets neurodegeneration: restoring lysosomal function with nanovectors.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Neurodegenerative diseases (NDs) remain a growing burden worldwide. Characterized primarily by degeneration of neurons in the central nervous system (CNS), driven in part by pathological protein aggregates and by alterations of the autophagy-lysosomal pathway (ALP), current therapeutic strategies only mitigate the outcomes of NDs rather than their origin, highlighting the need for the development of new targeted therapies. AREAS COVERED: CNS-targeted nanoparticles (NPs) to tackle ALP have offered promising avenues by bypassing biological barriers, reducing pathological protein aggregates, restoring lysosomal pH and activity, upregulating autophagic flux, and contributing to neuroprotection. This report summarizes recent advances in the development of CNS-Targeted nanocarriers for autophagy as a treatment for ND. EXPERT OPINION: Restoring ALP function is a promising disease-modifying strategy for NDs, as it helps clear toxic protein aggregates. Nanotechnology offers an effective way to deliver such therapies to the brain by overcoming the blood-brain barrier, enabling targeted, multimodal, and potentially cell-specific interventions. However, key challenges remain, including late diagnosis, the need for precise cell targeting, and concerns about long-term safety and bioaccumulation. Despite these limitations, growing research interest is expected to accelerate the development and clinical translation of these approaches.

articles.title: Editorial: Targeting dysregulation in metabolic diseases: potential therapeutic intervention.
Causal Exposure-Response Analysis: Estimands, Time-Varying Confounding, and the Parametric g-Formula.
articles.abstract: Exposure-response (ER) analysis often informs dose selection in clinical drug development, but the underlying causal assumptions are rarely made explicit. Exposure metrics commonly used in practice can have limitations: time-to-event metrics are outcome-dependent and can be causally incoherent; steady-state metrics can introduce immortal-time bias; and early metrics, while defensible, require unstated assumptions about later exposure or must be interpreted narrowly. Beyond metric selection, challenges persist even with ideal early or time-varying exposure metrics, as dose randomization protects against confounding only for the component of exposure variability driven by the assigned dose. On-treatment clinical variables can affect both exposure and response, inducing time-varying confounding that neither randomization, baseline adjustment, nor naive time-varying covariate adjustment can address. In this work, a directed acyclic graph (DAG) is used to formalize the causal structure and define the average causal exposure-response curve (ACERC) as the target estimand for ER analysis under time-varying confounding. The parametric g-formula is adapted to target this causal estimand and required assumptions are stated explicitly, including key consistency and no-multiple-versions-of-treatment (NMVT) assumptions, with implications for defining exposure metrics. Population pharmacokinetic (popPK) modeling serves an important role beyond computing exposure metrics, partially addressing the no-measurement-error assumption and enabling g-formula implementation via existing software. Two oncology-motivated simulation scenarios of dose-mediated and PK-mediated confounding illustrate the approach. A simulation study shows the g-formula recovers causal ER estimates where standard methods are inaccurate under the specified time-varying confounding. The two-step workflow combining popPK modeling with existing g-formula software is presented as a practical template for further development.
